easy.def: A place with games you play for fun.
examples: We went to the arcade.
The arcade has games.
I played a game at the arcade.

more.def: A place with lots of coin-operated games that people play for fun, or a covered walkway with shops along it.
examples: We played racing games at the arcade after the movie.
The arcade was full of flashing lights and music.
A long arcade of shops kept us dry in the rain.

easy.def: A curved shape over a door or a gate.
examples: We walked under the arch.
The door has an arch.
A stone arch is at the park.

more.def: A curved structure that spans an opening, such as the top of a door, a gate or a bridge.
examples: We walked through a stone arch into the old garden.
The bridge has three arches over the river.
A rainbow made a bright arch across the sky.

easy.def: To bend into a curve.
examples: The cat arches its back.
A rainbow arches across the sky.
He arched his eyebrow.

more.def: To bend or curve into a rounded shape.
examples: The cat arched its back and hissed at the dog.
A bridge arched over the river from one bank to the other.
She arched her eyebrows in surprise.

easy.def: A scientist who digs up old things to learn about the past.
examples: The archaeologist found a pot.
An archaeologist digs.
She is an archaeologist.

more.def: A scientist who digs up and studies old objects, such as pots and tools, to learn how people lived long ago.
examples: The archaeologist carefully brushed the dirt from the ancient clay pot.
An archaeologist found the remains of a Roman house.
The archaeologists dug in the desert for old tools.

easy.def: A very important leader in some churches.
examples: The archbishop spoke.
We saw the archbishop.
The archbishop wore a tall hat.

more.def: A high-ranking leader in some Christian churches who is in charge of many bishops.
examples: The archbishop gave a speech at the cathedral.
People gathered to hear the archbishop speak.
The archbishop wore a tall hat and a long robe.

easy.def: A person who plans buildings.
examples: The architect drew a plan.
An architect designed the house.
The architect made a model.

more.def: A person whose job is to design buildings.
examples: The architect drew a plan for the new school.
An architect designed the museum.
The architect made a small model of the tower.

easy.def: The way buildings are planned and made.
examples: I like the architecture of the old church.
She wants to study architecture.
The architecture of the castle is grand.

more.def: The art of planning and designing buildings, or the style in which a building is made.
examples: The tall towers and pointed roofs are typical of the architecture of old castles.
My aunt studied architecture so she could design schools and libraries.
The architecture of the museum made it look like a giant glass boat.

easy.def: A place where old papers and records are kept.
examples: The old maps are in the archives.
We visited the archives.
The archives keep records.

more.def: A place where important old papers, records and photos are stored, or the collection itself.
examples: The old maps of our town are kept in the city archives.
She searched the archives for photos of her great-grandparents.
The library's archives hold newspapers from a hundred years ago.

easy.def: A curved opening over a way in.
examples: We walked through the archway.
The archway is stone.
The garden has an archway.

more.def: A passage that has a curved top, like an arch.
examples: We walked under the stone archway.
The garden had an archway covered in roses.
A tall archway led into the castle.

easy.def: Very cold, like near the North Pole.
examples: The arctic wind blew.
Arctic foxes are white.
An arctic night.

more.def: Having to do with the very cold region around the North Pole, or extremely cold.
examples: The arctic fox has thick white fur that keeps it warm in the snow.
An arctic wind blew across the frozen lake.
Polar bears live in the arctic region.

easy.def: A part of a place.
examples: The play area is big.
This area is quiet.
We ate in the picnic area.

more.def: A part of a place or space.
examples: The playground has an area for little kids.
Rain fell over a large area of the state.
Please stay in the picnic area.

easy.def: The size of a flat surface.
examples: We measured the area of the rug.
A big room has a large area.
The area of the field is huge.

more.def: The amount of flat space inside a shape, measured in squares.
examples: The area of a square that is three feet on each side is nine square feet.
Find the area of the garden before buying grass seed.
The area of the football field is huge.

easy.def: A big place where games or shows are held.
examples: The arena was full.
We saw a game at the arena.
The arena is big.

more.def: A large building or space with seats around it, used for sports and shows.
examples: The arena was full of fans cheering for the team.
We watched the hockey game at the arena.
The circus performed in a large arena.

easy.def: To say you do not agree, sometimes in a mad way.
examples: My brother and I argue about who goes first.
Do not argue with your sister.
They argue about which show to watch.

more.def: To disagree with someone in words, or to give reasons for what you think.
examples: The two friends began to argue about the rules of the game.
The players argued with the referee about the call.
She argued that recess should be ten minutes longer.

easy.def: An angry talk between people who do not agree.
examples: They had an argument.
The argument was about a toy.
I had an argument with my brother.

more.def: A disagreement in which people say angry things about what they think.
examples: The two brothers had an argument about the game.
We settled the argument by taking turns.
They had an argument over who got the last cookie.

easy.def: A reason you give to show something is true.
examples: Her argument was clear.
He gave a good argument.
I made an argument for more recess.

more.def: A set of reasons that you give to try to show that something is right.
examples: She made a good argument for a longer recess.
The writer gave three arguments for planting trees.
His argument convinced the class.

easy.def: To start to happen.
examples: A problem arose.
A question arises.
A chance arose.

more.def: To begin to exist or happen, or to get up.
examples: A problem arose during the game.
A new question arises each day.
A chance arose to travel.

easy.def: Adding, taking away, multiplying and dividing numbers.
examples: I do arithmetic.
Arithmetic is math.
We learned arithmetic.

more.def: The part of math that deals with adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing numbers.
examples: We practiced arithmetic by adding and subtracting numbers.
Arithmetic is the basic part of math that uses numbers.
He does arithmetic in his head.

easy.def: A large boat in a very old story, which carried animals during a flood.
examples: Noah built an ark.
The ark floated on the water.
The animals went in the ark.

more.def: A large boat in an old story that was built to save a family and animals from a great flood.
examples: In the old story, Noah built an ark and filled it with animals.
We have a toy ark with pairs of animals.
The children's book showed an ark floating on a huge sea.

easy.def: The part of your body between your shoulder and your hand.
examples: Raise your arm.
My arm is strong.
She hugged me with both arms.

more.def: The long part of the body between the shoulder and the hand.
examples: He raised his arm to ask a question.
An octopus has eight arms.
The baby fell asleep in her mother's arms.

related.def: As much as your arms can hold.

easy.def: Having a weapon.
examples: The knight was armed with a sword.
The guards were armed.
He was armed with a spear.

more.def: Carrying a weapon, or equipped with something to protect or fight.
examples: The knight was armed with a sword and a shield.
The armed guards stood at the castle gate.
The explorers were armed with maps and lanterns.

easy.def: Metal clothes that protect a fighter.
examples: The knight wore armor.
The armor is shiny.
Armor is heavy.

more.def: A strong covering that protects the body, such as the metal suits that knights wore.
examples: The knight put on his heavy armor.
The armor was shiny and cold.
A turtle's shell is like armor.

easy.def: Covered with a hard layer to keep safe.
examples: The turtle has an armored shell.
An armored truck carries money.
The armadillo is an armored animal.

more.def: Covered with a strong layer of metal or hard plates for protection.
examples: The armored truck carried money from the bank to the vault.
Armadillos are armored animals, with bony plates across their backs.
The armored knight clanked across the courtyard.

easy.def: The part under your arm where it meets your body.
examples: He put the thermometer in his armpit.
I tucked the book under my armpit.
Wash your armpit.

more.def: The hollow place under your arm, where the arm meets the shoulder.
examples: He tucked the football under his armpit and ran.
The nurse put the thermometer under my armpit.
You should wash your armpits when you take a bath.

easy.def: A large group of soldiers.
examples: The army marched through the town.
An army guards the country.
Soldiers in the army wear uniforms.

more.def: A large, organized group of soldiers who fight on land.
examples: The army marched across the mountains.
A country's army protects its borders.
He joined the army after school.

easy.def: A nice smell.
examples: The aroma of bread.
A sweet aroma.
The aroma of coffee.

more.def: A pleasant, strong smell, especially of food or flowers.
examples: The aroma of fresh bread filled the kitchen.
The aroma of roses drifted across the garden.
We followed the delicious aroma to the bakery.

easy.def: On all sides of something, or in a circle.
examples: We sat around the fire.
The dog ran around the tree.
A fence is around the yard.

more.def: On every side of something, in a circle, or in different parts of a place.
examples: The planets travel around the sun.
We walked around the lake before lunch.
She looked around the room for her lost sock.

easy.def: Close by.
examples: Is anyone around?
Look around.
There are many birds around.

more.def: In the area nearby, or about a certain amount.
examples: There are not many people around early in the morning.
The class turned around when the door opened.
The game will begin at around noon.

easy.def: To put things in order.
examples: Arrange the books.
She arranged the flowers.
He arranges the chairs.

more.def: To put things in a certain order or position.
examples: Arrange the books by size.
She arranged the flowers in a vase.
He arranged the chairs in a circle.

easy.def: To plan.
examples: We arranged a picnic.
Mom arranged a ride.
He arranges the trip.

more.def: To plan or set up something ahead of time.
examples: Mom arranged a ride for us.
We arranged a picnic for Saturday.
The teacher arranged a field trip.

easy.def: The way things are put in order.
examples: The arrangement of the desks is new.
The flowers are in a nice arrangement.
The seating arrangement changed.

more.def: The way in which things are placed or put in order.
examples: The arrangement of the desks changed each month.
She made a pretty arrangement of flowers.
The seating arrangement put friends together.

easy.def: A big collection of things set out in order.
examples: There was an array of toys.
An array of colors.
A wide array of fruit.

more.def: A large group of things that are set out so that you can see them all, or a series of numbers in rows and columns.
examples: The shop had a wide array of colored pencils.
We learned to show multiplication with an array of dots in rows.
An array of cakes was spread out on the table.

easy.def: To catch a person who did something against the law.
examples: The police arrested the thief.
An officer arrested the man.
They arrest people who break the law.

more.def: To catch someone and hold them because they are thought to have broken the law.
examples: The police arrested the man who stole the bike.
Officers arrest people who break the law.
The sheriff arrested the thief at the train station.

easy.def: Coming to a place.
examples: The arrival of the bus was late.
We waited for her arrival.
The arrival of spring is soon.

more.def: The act of reaching a place.
examples: The arrival of the train was five minutes late.
We waited for the arrival of our guests.
The arrival of spring brings flowers.

easy.def: To get to a place.
examples: We arrive at noon.
The bus arrived.
She arrived at school.

more.def: To reach a place after traveling.
examples: We arrived at the campsite just before dark.
The train arrives at four o'clock.
Grandma arrived with a big bag of presents.

easy.def: Thinking you are better than others.
examples: The arrogant prince bragged.
He is arrogant.
An arrogant smile.

more.def: Too proud and acting as if you are more important than other people.
examples: The arrogant prince bragged about his gold.
He was arrogant and would not listen.
The arrogant cat looked down at the dog.

easy.def: A sign that points the way.
examples: Follow the arrow.
The arrow points left.
The arrow shows the exit.

more.def: A sign shaped like a line with a point at the end, used to show a direction.
examples: Follow the arrow on the sign.
The arrow points to the exit.
A red arrow showed us which way to turn.

easy.def: A thin stick shot from a bow.
examples: The arrow hit the target.
The archer shot an arrow.
He held an arrow.

more.def: A thin, straight stick with a point, shot from a bow.
examples: The archer shot an arrow at the target.
The arrow flew through the air.
He pulled an arrow from his quiver.

easy.def: Drawing, painting and other things you make.
examples: I love art class.
Art is fun.
Her art is on the wall.

more.def: Pictures, sculptures and other things that people make to show ideas or feelings.
examples: The art in the museum is hundreds of years old.
We painted flowers in art class.
She loves music, dance and art.

easy.def: A piece of writing in a newspaper or magazine.
examples: I read an article about space.
The article had a picture.
She wrote an article.

more.def: A piece of writing in a newspaper, magazine or website about a certain subject.
examples: The newspaper ran an article about the new park.
Our class read an article about whales.
He wrote an article for the school paper.

easy.def: A thing.
examples: A hat is an article of clothing.
He lost an article.
This is a useful article.

more.def: One single thing, especially one of a group of things.
examples: A coat is an article of clothing.
The lost article was returned to its owner.
Each article in the box was wrapped in paper.

easy.def: An old thing made by people long ago.
examples: The museum has an artifact.
They found an artifact.
The artifact is old.

more.def: An object made by people long ago that is studied to learn about the past.
examples: The museum has artifacts from ancient Egypt, such as pottery and jewelry.
Archaeologists found an old stone tool and called it an artifact.
The clay pot was an artifact from a village that lived here long ago.

easy.def: Made by people, not by nature.
examples: The flowers are artificial.
We have an artificial tree at Christmas.
This juice has artificial color.

more.def: Made by people and not found in nature; not real.
examples: The pond was an artificial lake built for the park.
An artificial leg helped him run and play sports.
The plant on the desk is artificial, so it never needs water.

easy.def: A person who makes art.
examples: The artist paints pictures.
My mom is an artist.
The artist used bright colors.

more.def: A person who creates art, such as paintings or music.
examples: The artist painted a picture of the sea.
A street artist drew pictures with chalk.
My aunt is an artist who makes clay pots.

easy.def: Good at art.
examples: She is artistic.
An artistic drawing.
He has artistic skill.

more.def: Having a talent for art or showing a love of beauty.
examples: She is artistic and loves to paint.
The garden was an artistic mix of colors.
He has an artistic eye for photos.

easy.def: Painting, music, dance and other creative subjects.
examples: I like the arts.
We study the arts at school.
The arts are fun.

more.def: Creative subjects and activities such as painting, music, dancing and drama.
examples: I take part in the arts after school.
The school has a strong program in the arts.
Music and drama are part of the arts.

easy.def: Pictures and things that people make as art.
examples: The artwork is colorful.
We hung our artwork.
Her artwork is on the wall.

more.def: Paintings, drawings and other things that people make as art.
examples: Our class hung our artwork in the hallway.
The museum has artwork from many countries.
Her artwork won a prize at the fair.
